Relations among contents, self-location, affect, temporal organization, and other dimensions within experience.
The degree to which differentiated experiential contents belong to one coordinated phenomenal field.
The degree to which distinguishable experiential contents remain non-identical within a phenomenal field.
The organization by which features or contents are experienced as belonging together within one object, event, or field.
A graded magnitude of an experiential quality under a declared measurement/report scheme.
The experienced clarity or richness of phenomenal content, separable from factual accuracy and report confidence.
A discrepancy between experiences in a declared multidimensional phenomenological state space.
A mapping that assigns distances or discrepancies among phenomenal states and must demonstrate cross-context stability to support metric language.
The organized pattern of similarities, differences, trajectories, and constraints among phenomenal states.
The phenomenal character by which an experience is presented as belonging to this subject or self.
The system-relative character of experience as occurring for a particular subject; used cautiously as a phenomenological descriptor.
The perspectival organization from which a world and body are experienced or represented.
A stabilized relational centre relative to which contents are organized as here, now, and for this subject.
The experienced immediacy or current givenness of content in the phenomenal field.
The experiential extension of the present through retention of just-past states and anticipation of near-future possibilities.
The structured succession of phenomenal states in which continuity and change coexist.
The property by which a mental or phenomenal state is directed toward or about an object, state, proposition, or possibility; distinct from intention as future-directed goal constraint.
Availability of information for reasoning, flexible control, report, and action under an access-based usage.
Consciousness considered specifically as there-being-something-it-is-like, analytically distinct from cognitive access.
An experimental design seeking markers of conscious processing without requiring an explicit report on every trial.
The mapping from internal states and task demands to overt reports; it can change without identical changes in phenomenality.
A first-person description or structured rating of experience treated as fallible measurement data.
Phenomenological measurement using multiple dimensions, relations, or trajectories rather than a single binary report.
A reported alteration or reduction of ordinary self-boundary/self-model organization; mechanisms vary and the term is phenomenological, not a unitary diagnosis.
A reported alteration in the sense of self, ownership, or reality of self-experience; clinical interpretation requires independent assessment.
A reported alteration in the felt reality or presence of the external world; mechanisms and diagnoses must not be inferred from the label alone.
Organization in which bodily states, sensorimotor contingencies, and regulation participate in self-model and cognition.
A representation or measurement of current body-related variables at a declared physiological or computational level.
The self-model components grounded in body ownership, body schema, interoception, proprioception, and sensorimotor relation.
An internal representation of body properties used for prediction, control, localization, or interpretation.
A sensorimotor organization of body position and action possibilities, often operating without explicit reflection.
The sense or attribution that a body or body part belongs to oneself; experimentally manipulable and distinct from self-location.
The attribution that an action was produced by oneself, distinguishable from mere movement detection.
The represented distinction between self-related and environment-related states.
Persistence of the self-world distinction under changing sensory, bodily, and social conditions.
A system-relative reference point used to organize spatial, bodily, and first-person relations.
Sensing or representation of internal bodily states.
Availability or awareness of internal bodily signals, which may vary independently of objective interoceptive accuracy.
Performance on tasks designed to estimate correspondence between reported/detected internal bodily signals and a reference measure.
Sensing of body position and movement from muscles, joints, and related signals.
Sensing of states or events external to the body through sensory systems.
Information related to balance, acceleration, and head/body orientation.
Regulation that maintains selected internal variables within viable ranges.
Predictive or anticipatory regulation that adjusts internal control in expectation of changing demands.
Maintenance of body-related constraints relevant to viability and self-preservation.
A regular relation linking action to expected changes in sensory input.
